verdict.rationale: The evidence shows Vue ships first-party, officially supported state stores rather than relying on third parties. The docs link Pinia, and community users say Vue "provides an official router and store called Vuex" with "no need to resort to third parties." However, these are separate official packages, and nothing documents managing global state with core built-in reactivity primitives alone. One community comment also raises modularity concerns about using Vuex as a global. Missing for 10: documentation of core built-in primitives (e.g. reactive state shared across components) used for global state without an extra package, and in-depth first-party docs on the state management pattern.
